task:
Are you the <Ranger>? Wonderful, I think our offer will be interesting for you. Mr. Brigee Bardozze's xenopark housing xenomorphs (the Peleng term for rare animals) from all over the Galaxy is very popular on planet <ToPlanet>. Rabby Terezze, the chief xenopark feeder, asked us for help. Unfortunately, some... errr..., problems with the customs will make him stay on <FromPlanet> for some time and he says that the automatic feeder battery charge will be enough for <Day> days only. We propose that you go onto <ToPlanet> and assume Mr. Terezze's responsibilities in the xenopark for that period of time. We suspect that Mr. Bardozze's generosity will be surprisingly nice. Of course, you will get your fee only if all Brigee Bardozze's pets are alive by the chief feeder's arrival.

But note - the automatic feeder will stop functioning in <Day> days, if not earlier, and then all the xenomorphs will die of hunger. So you must be there before it happens and save them.
success: Dear <Ranger>, thank you very much for saving Brigee Bardozze's xenomorphs! Here is the check for <Money> cr, which is about 10% of Brigee Bardozze's yearly income produced by the xenopark. We hope for your future fruitful co-operation with the Peleng race!
loc.1.0:
You hardly killed your ship's engines when a rather presentable aerocar with the <clr> "Brigee Bardozze's xenopark "<clrEnd> sticker on its side drove to the ship. It looked like they had kept their promise to meet you. You left the ship and approached the aerocar. After the check/X-ray/search-everything-possible procedure, which was quite usual for Peleng planets, you felt rather uncomfortable.

- Are you <Ranger>? Rabby sent you, right? - a young Peleng asked popping out of the car. He was obviously very excited. After your positive answer his face lit with joy.
- At last! We thought you wouldn't to make it. The situation with the xenomorphs is extremely bad. Make haste!!! It's been two days already since the autofeeder's battery ran out and we are completely desperate.

You sat into the car and it sailed up into the cloud rushing to the east with the maximum speed. 
    
- The xenopark is out of town - animals are different, you know, - your guide explained.
- Did you experience any accidents?
- No, thank goodness - we just care for our neighbours here, on <ToPlanet>, and don't want to bother them, and living in the vicinity of xeno...
- There will be some... - you interrupted the Peleng in mid-sentence, - So you are Rabby Terezze's assistant, aren't you? 
- Oh, yes. Here... he got in touch with me and asked me to pass these books to you...

With that he handed you two electronic booklets:
<clr> Food for Xenomorphs of our Galaxy <clrEnd>
<clr>Behaviour and Brief Description of Xenomorphs <clrEnd>
loc.4.0:
You leafed the books the chief feeder's assistant had given to you. "Food for xenomorphs..." turned out to be something like a manual for alien animal feeding, and "Behaviour..." contained notes by different hunters and scholars about the hunting for valuable species and descriptions. Did you really want to stuff your head with that junk?

You put the books aside and spent the rest of the flight gazing out of the window. The speed twice as supersonic turned the <ToPlanet>'s landscapes into multicoloured blurs that were flitting along.

At last the aerocar landed on the lawn in front of the huge building. You got out of the car and the feeder's assistant flung the door admitting to the yard open:
- Welcome, dear <Ranger>...

A pale, or...rather, a light-green, well...even a light-yellow Peleng appeared from behind the side door clasping...something. That something was squealing and stinking and looked very much like one of xenopark's pets.

- Are you the promised xenomorph-feeding expert? - the something's master asked. - I'm happy you've come at last - the animals feel completely awful already... And I'm afraid, it all became even more complicated now. This young sploshling, - he pointed to the strange creature in his hands that stopped squealing but was diffusing the same reek, unfortunately, - he decided to play a little bit and disarranged all the tablets on the cages. So now we don't know which feed should go where. Not to make the matter worse, we left everything as it was - may be some of the tablets had remained on their places...
- What do you mean? Don't you even know what animal lives in what cage?!!
- Unfortunately, we have just one xenomorph expert. And we are just clerks and traders. Mr. Bardozze is hep to all these freaks as well but he left for Cvanarians a week ago and we don't expect him back soon. And you know, we hate to bother him with such trifles - we heard you are a competent expert. So, are you ready?

loc.5.0:
You forced the books into the clerk's hands and strode to the aerocar murmuring:

No way! It's not just feeding these beasts but playing that damn "Nick the animal" game thing. I'll nick that animal after it bites me just once... Faugh! Let me just get back to <FromPlanet>, I'll give that xenomorph feeding expert a doing!!!

The feeder's assistant drew up with you right at the car:
- What a pity! It looks like poor creatures will starve to death, and we'll take the knock... Good bye. I think you better stay away from <ToPlanet> - the locals won't have any desire to deal with the individual who deprived them of such an entertainment and doomed these harmless xenomorphs to dying of hunger... Good bye, harmless animal blighter - all the population of our sector will know that due to you, <Ranger>, there appeared several more items in the Incarnadine Talmud.
- Wipe your light-green ass with this Incarnadine Talmud! Go find another expert!
loc.6.0:
You entered a big room. There are five cages with all kinds of beasts to your left. And seven tubs with some hockey, which probably was the food for the xenomorphs.

What will you do? The tablets are disarranged and you can't make mistakes and should give each creature the food it needed... There is just one nice thing - there are piles of food in the tubs. And all the tablets are on their places; at least that was what the caretaker said... The latter was strange, to say the least, considering the Peleng's meanness and perverted sense of humour.
loc.7.0: You're standing at Cage №1 with the tablet <clr>"Big habbath. Planet Taboth "<clrEnd> on it.

loc.12.0: So, what book do you want to hive wisdom from?
loc.13.0:
You opened the book <clr>"Behaviour and brief description of xenomorphs "<clrEnd>.
There are five different chapters, each containing the description of one animal from the xenopark. The information is provided in text view or in audiorecords. Rather, these are not descriptions but just stories about how these species were found told by those who were the first to come across them.

What xenomorph do you want to know about?
loc.13.1:
My detachment was proud of the fact that it was its members who came across the most dangerous predator whose ferocious violence and unusual strength could be the symbol of the Maloq race and its undeletable might.

That merciless enemy killed one half of the detachment. Due to its incredible skill to disguise in the Taboth Mountains, the habbath took our scouting detachment at advantage. But the need of the Maloq treasury in Taboth sapphires for the war budget increase exceeded the fear of the beast. Yes, it was fear because the worthiest fighters, the pick of the army, were buried under the Taboth copper sun. All of them had been found with slit sculls near the rocks where habbaths lived. It became clear since then that we had come across a worthy and very strong enemy. And we tasted of fear for the first time and don't blush to own it.

But the most incredible thing was his complete scorn of death that is very typical of habbaths. Surrounded by exceeding forces, the enemy didn't run but just laughed scornfully. Even torture didn't break him - it laughed in the face of torture, and that laughter is still ringing in my ears: "hyr-hyr-hrr-ha!"

Habbath! This is the beast that should become the symbol of the Maloq nation, its strength, greatness, and fearlessness, associated with swordskills and invincibility of the Maloq army.
loc.13.2:
Swamp phatklink is the most rare type of phatklinks and the most interesting one for historians and pelengists because there is every reason to believe that it is these swamp phatklinks who were home pets of the great race, Shmelengs, our ancestors ages ago. Some scholars even think that the Pelengs are descendants of phatklinks and to prove it, they mention the fact that the swamp phatklink also has four arms. This is a serious argument but they forget that phatklinks have no legs at all whereas Pelengs have two of them...

   Swamp phatklinks were only found on three planets: in Big Cataracts on Luptzvack, in Big Swales on Chvack, and in Huge Plumper on Small Uprat. These are the planets where cultural remains of ancient Shmeleng civilisation were found.

   The swamp phatklink is an extremely good swimmer and spends almost all of his life in the water. His flashy lips and teeth make a filter of a kind that strains swamp water to find phlies, the phatklinks' favourite food. Due to their strong and long paws, phatklinks can make large leaps chasing sucklings or female phatklinks.

These amusing animals are easily trained and this fact just verifies their former pet history, plus they are so nice to pat...
loc.13.3:
It all started as usual - ranger Anton, Schulman and me surrounded that Klissan and struck simultaneously. And, cut him up to the state of [censored]. And suddenly a passage to the hyper opens and so this green piece of scum [censored] Penzquack - [cenozred] him and his [cencored] four-handed kin, and loads all of the protoplasma on board of his ship. Well me and the lads we got upset you know, so we chased him into the hyper and we whaled'im good so that this green [censored] pees every time he hears the word "protoplasm".

    Well, the most interesting thing about this - right in the middle of this freaking pile of protoplasma we found this little beast here. It was sitting there, munching on something that looked like a protobladder - almost finished it by that time, it did... or maybe it was a gillnozzle... Well, that's not important. At first I thought it was a Klissan - I mean, we never seen'em before. So, methinks, why the hell would we want to capture their ships intact, when all the fatherland wants is protoplasma, right? But as it turned out we were mistaken. Turned out to be some beast of theirs - it was. So Schulman says - "What if we whack'im with this plasmagun, eh?" And Anton goes: "Back off, Schulman, if you could have things your way you'd whack the entire universe with plasmaguns, you would! I say let's plasmack it with this whacker..."

Well, to cut a long story short - they could be going like that for ages, like a couple of them old geezers on a bench, you know, but then this little scumdog runs over to me and starts rubbing itself against me leg. Well, I felt sorry for it, couldn't help it really... I mean I had them new overalls on, and I hardly managed to wash that slime off, y'know... And this six-legged beast keeps rubbing against me leg, just like your dog would. Then next thing you know it already only has four legs. No, Cap, we don't drink before the raids... Anyway, we are all quite surprised at seeing this dog has five legs, you know, and then Schulman goes: 
- Remember that brandy we got from Schpook? It was all foul, you know! I told ya, we should of been chasing Lapack, but you lot kept whining: "let's help the diplomat... let's help the diplomat"! 

So we all think, wassup with that, what's got into him, the food was good - you know, that sea rapitzuck caviar thing, and then we looks at that dog - gee, what a hideous sight she was! All green, three-legged, sits there and winks at us, you know. Ye gods, I be beggared if I take a system liberation mission after that guy's birthday party again... No way, I'd be better off puking all over this spaceship 'cause of being space-sick, then freak out at the sight of this green stump. Nah, Cap'n, we ain't been drinkin', we 'aven't...
loc.13.4:
In the context of speculative theosophistry, Aishout is identified with a singular reservoir of coapsular bioenergetics, and this fact proves it's harmonious co-existence with the ether of the Faeyaton planet where this unique species of deeply intelligent vegetable life was found. 
    The research made by Gaalian ihike-bahanists showed that this plant is the concentration of wisdom, because it is obviously involved in the self-meditative process of searching after the philosophical ego. The level of harmonious rhythming with Nirvana is so high, that even Aishout juveniles hardly react at all our scholars' attempts of contacting them. The unique self-patterning and harmonious co-existence with the light of celestial energy concentrations..."

...As far as you understood, it meant that like all plants, Aishouts synthesised all substances necessary for their existence in the light only.

"...on the level of quantum interpenetration allows us to put some philosophical substance under the study of the ancient Gaalian scholar, Peehee-Phiga-Gohor in the name, who said "Das ist or not to ist", which is: 
"Everything that truly exists can't but exist, harmoniously co-existing with other truly existing individuals whose true existence is the truth laid into the supreme structures of universe..."

...This phrase made you stuporous for a long time, and only half a pail of cold water poured on you brought you to yourself.

"...and direct evidence of the fact that the supreme nous exists in the very phluctual hypostasis that was mentioned in the works of the great Gaalian philosopher, Krahan-T by name, who said "Ahtung schneller - zig Hitler kaput", which is:
  "There is no nous that penetrates the phantasmal universe and is greater in its ether hypostasis than..." You realised that if you read further, you " will synchronise your rhythm with the rhythm of schizophrenically justified idiocy to the level of singular phase ".

However, one phrase underlined in red, attracted your attention:

"...The largeness of the inner meditativeness is based not only on the substantial size of the universe noesis visual instrument, but also on plenty of expanded in space organs of rythmisation with the beating of the universe ether nous (we call these organs leaves); the quantity of them is equal to the number of the satellites travelling around the Ohokany planet whose ideally spherical shape is equivalent to the visual image of Faeyaton's black sun, and the latter fact is just one more evidence of..."

You remember flying by that planet once - surely, it had four satellites... or three, but by no means two or five...
loc.13.5:
A special necessity brought us to this red planet: these dirty looters, stinky custom rats from Venus somehow considered our excellent heroino-marihuanic cigars to be contraband and confiscated the freight! Fortunately enough, they failed to find the LSD -120 Dryck consignment that we were planning to sell at the best on Mars.
   
Heat and lack of water influenced the immoral image of my gang a lot... I mean, team, oh yes, team. Those harriers from the Water supplying station opened their mouth so wide naming the price for a jug of water that I feel awkward now calling myself a pirate. Did I say pirate? I meant a trader, of course. But the meeting with the Ship or the Sand Ship, as the pale-skinned locals call it, was the most horrible experience.

Although his muzzle reminded a noble Peleng profile, the awful colour of its skin just screamed, and the skin itself touched... ough! I'd rather pat an ohlalaian greedorshroom. The absence of arms will make the description of the Sand Ship complete and the beast's full image will be a damper to your desire to sleep for a long time. In spite of all this, it felt completely confident in the Martian sands and we used it as a pack animal... ough!, I still can't make my mind of touching this beast's nasty skin. To pack it was our punishment for misbehaviour...

...No!!! Don't, mister officer, I'll never do it again. This is not my freight, and I have no idea how it came that my fingerprints are on it! This is not my ship at all - I'm an honest Peleng!!! I clean forgot how I landed up in it... I don't even remember my name!!! Mummy, mummy - agoo-goo, I wanna a sweetzie!!! Officer, anything but shooting - I will complain to the Association of Killers!
loc.14.0: You approached the right wall with seven huge tubs at it, which are tightly topped. There are tablets with names on them. The local care-keeper assured you that the sploshling didn't mix them up so the substances in the tubs coincide with the tablets. But it doesn't make the whole situation easier...
loc.15.0:
You opened the book <clr>"Food for xenomorphs of our Galaxy"<clrEnd>, rather, it was not a book but a number of separate files containing the following information:

1. Vitamin B-685 is necessary to maintain life of <clr>the phatklink<clrEnd>. It is contained in the stems of swamp heather or extracted in scraps from the marrow of Stalomian Gabosauruses. However, the latter are as rare as phatklinks themselves.

2. <clr>The Aishout<clrEnd> prefers refined food with high content of carbohydrates and carbon dioxide to synthesise glucose and sucrose, which are the most important components of Aishout's vegetable organism. The reason for Aishouts' extinction was their eating quality for aborigines who made flour high in carbohydrates out of their stems.

3. All types of <clr>Ships<clrEnd> feed only on vegetable food containing slightly sour liquids (juices) or liquid food because they live in hyporhumid conditions. They can do without water and food for a long time.

4. As any other raptor, <clr>Proto-shpock<clrEnd> feeds on organic flash of killed animals; in captivity it is possible to feed it with saturated live organics - the inner processes of the beast should stay active. It ignores passive organics but can eat non-organic compounds though it causes irreversible changes of the animal's DNA.

5. <clr>Habbaths<clrEnd> feed on the ground Sun nonstone that strengthen their armour. Unfortunately, ground Sun nonstone hardly exists in the nature, which brings to Habbaths' dying-out due to their inability to digest solid food. So to feed a captive habbath it is necessary to ground the Sun nonstone.

<clr>Caution! While feeding the animals, one should keep in mind the following - they don't ignore ALL types of food that are improper for them and can make a mistake and eat something different from what they must get. This food might be either completely harmless for them or, vice versa, turn out to be a deadly poison or cause serious disease.
In case of food poisoning the habitual food helps the sick animal to overcome crisis and it recovers <clrEnd>.
loc.16.0: Before the beasts got off the hooks starving, you should hurry up and decide what feed will go where. The hell of the thing is that you can't make mistakes. You stay thinking in front of the tubs. What beast is kept in Cage №1 and what does it feed on?
loc.16.1: You took a bunch of Noohoo-Dle and put it in the manger. The animal <clr>ignored <clrEnd> your true attempts to save its life.
loc.16.2: The animal tremulously flicked out its mug to the drinking bowl and started lapping it. You were about to sigh with relief but suddenly it started desperately hissing and spitting up. It looked like the xenomorph <clr>got poisoned<clrEnd>.
loc.16.3: You took a handful of sparkling small crystals and emptied it into the manger. You could as well have made a striptease show - <clr>no heed<clrEnd> to either you, or sparklings. The only emotion you could see in its eyes was scorn worthy of the Great Lyakusha himself.
loc.16.4: You threw the lid open and dipped up some of the criambusine with a trowel. Then you carefully approached the cage, tipped the half-liquid mass into the manger, and started watching. The beast came to the manger, nosed it and <clr>turned away with disgust <clrEnd>. You completely agreed with it. Well, this creature demonstrated its absolute reluctance to eat criambusine...
loc.16.5: You tipped a handful of globules from Tub 3 and handed it to the beast. The animal nosed the feed lazily and <clr>and indifferently turned away <clrEnd>. Failure.

loc.17.1: You put a prickly sprig near the creature. It bent its head over the "rind-blooming" and stood motionless. Than the wide paws started raking out the soil under the sprig with the palpus. When a shallow hole was ready, the beast <clr>swept the feed into the hole and powdered it with the soil<clrEnd>.
loc.17.2:
You threw several globules at the animal that caught them speedily. It chewed up the farinose feed and even got a little bit lighter. <clr>There appeared some content in the beast's eyes <clrEnd>. Or did it just seem to you? It ate several more globules with the same speed but something is obviously lacking - it doesn't take any more globules and is just looking at you expectantly.

It looks like the beast feeds on something else too...
loc.17.3: You poured some of that bubbled liquid into a bowl and put it near the beast. It bent over the bowl <clr>showing some interest<clrEnd> and stared expectantly at you... Probably, it wants something else.
loc.17.4:
You threw several globules at the animal that caught them speedily. It chewed up the farinose feed and even got a little bit lighter. There appeared some content in the beast's eyes. Or did it just seem to you? It ate several more globules with the same speed but something is obviously lacking - it doesn't take any more globules and is just looking at you expectantly. It <clr>obviously feels better and recovered from the poisoning <clrEnd>. 

It looks like the beast feeds on something else too...
loc.17.5: The creature in the cage <clr>ignored<clrEnd> the long stems or what-ever-it-was.
loc.17.6: You took a sparkling and threw it to the monster. Its thin neck curved and the animal adroitly caught the sparkling with its chaps. But some time after it spat it out. <clr>The transparent liquid with pharmacy fume that served the creature as blood was dripping out of its wounded chaps <clrEnd>.
loc.17.7: It took you much effort to pick out a piece of "photons", which you threw into the cage. The animal flustered as if you had thrown a burning sprig there - it pulled up its...roots?!! out of the soil with loathsome spat and <clr> hurriedly crawled away from the photons <clrEnd> on its wide palpi.

loc.18.2: You put some globules into the manger. The creature reached a couple of them with its tongue but <clr>spat them out<clrEnd> immediately. Well, at least it didn't fell.

loc.19.1:
You will never understand these creatures - you hardly held your hand out when the animal rolled to you and grasped the Noohoo-Dle with its either trunk, or palpus that appeared as if growing out from the body. After the beast sucked the wriggling rods in, it stared at you with its large platelike eyes.
   - What else do you want, aquamarine whangdoodle? - you asked but the blueskinned creature kept silent. At least, <clr>it doesn't look like dying <clrEnd>.
loc.19.2: You hardly went away from the cage when the creature rolled up to the scattering of sparklings and scrambled it up in a pile with its either trunk, or palpus that appeared as if growing out from the body. Probably, it's not just love of the beautiful but <clr>part of the creature's ration <clrEnd>. But what else does it need then?
loc.19.3: You are good at throwing and the creature is a good sleeper and <clr>is completely ignoring <clrEnd> the crisp globules. Your attempt to feed it failed.
loc.19.4: The animal <clr>paid no attention <clrEnd> to the whole bunch of appetising thorny branches.
loc.19.5: It took you a lot of effort to pick out a piece, which the creature just <clr>ignored<clrEnd> as if it had been elementary photons... What a pity!
loc.19.6: The only thing you managed to do was <clr>dirtying the beast's light-blue skin <clrEnd>.
loc.20.0: Before the beasts got off the hooks starving, you should hurry up and decide what feed will go where. The hell of the thing is that you can't make mistakes. You stay thinking in front of the tubs. What beast is kept in Cage № 5 and what does it feed on?
loc.20.1:
You were prickling and crying but the animal was stubborn and refused to scoff that thorny plant. But you only needed to go away from the cage and the animal slowly approached the pile of thorns and chewed up a couple of branches. What happened next was even worse than a nightmare: suddenly the creature gathered up, than got back to its normal shape. The same thorns like those on the branches grew up through its scale and its two front legs turned into something like nippers.

It looks like <clr>the animal is completely unwell <clrEnd>... At least, you haven't taken LSD-400, so the problem is in the wrong feeding.
loc.20.2: All for nothing - the animal <clr>didn't even pay any attention <clrEnd> to the feeding.
loc.20.3: The animal <clr>glanced indifferently<clrEnd> at the pile of crystals. Failure.
loc.20.4: You hardly put the criambusine on the floor when the six-legged beast ran up to the feeding pile left by you and sent the sticky mass flying at one of the lamps with a powerful throw. The dirty lamp stopped shining. The creature immediately moved to the shadow and started changing its appearance before your very eyes - the scale covered with blebs and pungent slime started dribbling out of them. The xenomorph itself <clr>enlarged twice in size <clrEnd>. You didn't take hazards and refused to give it any more of criambusine - God knows what it will do next then.
loc.21.0:
You came closer to the cage and started watching the creature in it. 

What you saw was huge - at least, it was the biggest animal you had met there. About two meters in height, the monster was covered with short hard tawny (like a brown stone) fur. The animal's knobby muscles redoubled that resemblance of the stone. Its long thick neck was slightly curving - the animal slowly looked about noticing every single detail. Simultaneously its big lips moved as if whispering or chewing something. The animal walked around the cage completely ignoring you. Its strong muscled legs finished in wide and hard heel surely able to crumble stone. Two skinny sinewed outgrowths on the animal's back redoubled the impression of invincible force. Judging from their thickness (they were scarcely lower than the head), those outgrowths protected the animal as well as a horny test would do.

The creature was slowly shifting from one foot to the other. The floor of the cage was covered by small gravel-stone, in the corners there stood rock spalls. The light of a small yellow sun-imitator was severe and almost blinded you. "A high-powered thing, damn it", - you thought.

Suddenly the animal turned its heat to you and... spat directly into your face! "Hrrr", - the beast snorted. Shouting you rushed to the washstand to wash that sure as death dangerous substance off your face. Well, at least, the creature doesn't suffer from the deficiency of liquid in it.
loc.22.0:
A strange purple creature was sitting in the dreadful shade of the cage. Its big head on an extremely long and thin neck, which ran into the body almost with no changes in thickness, was turning to you like a locator. Four wide, flat... palpuses, moved without stopping including those two that served for footing to remain in vertical position. 

Wide chaps full of small but very sharp teeth and a couple of big black beads serving as eyes redoubled the dreadful impression of the beast's appearance. Its rough skin crackled after each move putting you in more fear. 

The creature's limbs dipped into the cloudy puddle nearby and it took the xenomorph some time to move them there as if trying to catch something. Then it took them out with a loud smack. The beast didn't make a sound and remained motionless all that time; only quiet crackling of the rough skin could be heard in the shaded cage.
loc.24.0:
You came closer to the cage. There was a strange, completely motionless creature in it. It looked very much like a granite blue mass, half of you in height. Large dark blue plate like eyes were staring at you. The creature remained motionless and didn't make a sound, even when you made a scary face at it.

Suddenly you sneezed - the creature coiled itself into a ball, rolled away to the far corner of the cage and... fell asleep. You could even hear that amazing creature's snoring. Try as you would to distinguish its arms or legs, you failed. It wasn't even clear if it was an animal or a strange plant.

You spat on the sand covering the floor of the cage and turned away. The ominous red sun created some imminent atmosphere. You approached the mirror and made a face again - it was really scary! You even started looking about after each sound and didn't come up to the mirror again.
loc.35.0:
You shut your eyes tight, dipped up a handful of criambusine and shoved it into your mouth. You tried to chew it but your teeth agglutinated and sand crisped on them. After a desperate effort you swallowed that mass, but one clot got fast in your throat barring the air. Choking, you crawled to the emergency button and banged it like grim death.

The cluttered staff found you writhing in agony on the floor. The local aide, the veterinarian, to be more precise, quickly understood what was going on and gave you a flask with spirit. The 99% potion burnt your throat but the clot dissolved letting you enjoy the stale air of the xenopark.

After that vexatious incident they put you in the hospital and you failed to help the poor xenomorphs. While you were there, the owner of the xenopark, mister Bardozze, visited you himself and hinted that your future staying on <ToPlanet> might tell on your health because the only xenopark in the whole <ToStar> system and its owner went down drain. His last phrase was the last straw that broke the camel's back and made you laugh hysterically:
- You are a right one scoffing criambusine... Do you know what it is? I guess, you don't! This is food for the swamp phatklink: 30% of kurayaba, or swamp heather, and 70% of swamp mess itself.
loc.36.0:
There is the following superscription on Tub №1: 
<clr>VAZZE CRIAMBUSINE <clrEnd>

This criambusine looks very unappetising. Actually... like excrements. Half-liquid clotted heterogeny, grey, brown, and green in colour, mixed with some light-green plants. Every 2-3 minutes fist-sized bubbles swelled and burst on the surface. After you looked at the mess, the half-digested patty with penchekryak stuffing moved in your stomach.

Venturing upon a trailblazing experiment, you smelled the criambusine. Its smell reminded you of carrion straw with a faint tincture of rotten eggs or saliva of Gaelinian mibser. You went farther and placed your finger into it. Really, it was the vazze criambusine (though honestly you had no idea what criambusina was made of). Warm, half-liquid... rather sticky and can hardly be removed, especially, from the shirt. And from the trousers too, as it turned out later. But obviously not excrements, judging from the smell.
loc.36.1: You recollected your courage and licked your finger. Then you tried to chew that mass but when you felt sand on your teeth, you decided to better swallow it. It made neither worse, nor better. Its taste was a strange mixture of paraffin and sand with carrion grass. It obviously was neither nutritious nor tasty.
loc.36.2: You slightly licked your fingertip feeling insecure. A slightly warm mass tasted like... paraffin? Samaldock niuphtiuline? It was not enough to figure out. However, it was not poisonous for you.
loc.37.0:
There is the following superscription on Tub №2:
<clr>Quack-Tose Rind-blooming<clrEnd>

These Quacks are obviously plants and look very much like mercipane oleasterous, an ornamental popular with Maloq housewives. Though the latter doesn't have such thorns. Furthermore, Quack turned out to be shrilly green, which is rather rare among plants (or animals?). Whatever it was, but the animal, which is able to eat THAT together with the thorns, should have a tin throat and a tin stomach. Though probably, it has an external digestive system and it just dissolves thorns.

That warped plant with few dry leaves strewed with sharp thorns didn't seem tasty to you though you obviously knew the smell... where from, you wondered?
loc.37.1: You took a small sprig without thorns on it and chewed it. Memories rushed upon you. Of course! You knew that taste very well! Now you knew for sure how the plant they make your favourite Vtequila of looks like. The best wash-belly all over the Galaxy! Oh, thank you very much, dear Quack-Tose, for what you are!
loc.37.2:
You broke off a small sprig and licked it...
Dear me!!! What a pain! A sharp long thorn stuck in your tongue, which immediately got puffed.

When the pain was gone, you carefully dripped one drop of the juice that was dribbling from the fissure on your tongue. Its taste turned out to be slightly sour and acerb. It was familiar too but the quantity was not enough to figure out.
loc.45.0:
Feeling happy after you chanced upon such a nice attribute of that plant, you lit into it playing a good knife and fork. In the beginning of the process you took some effort and tried to break off thorns but after some time you didn't care any longer.

Stupidly giggling, you were hopping along the room, making faces to the poor animals that turned out to be doubled somehow in their cages. Sharp thorns were sticking in your tongue, throat and might have already scratched your stomach but you felt no pain, just marvellous lightness and sweet euphoria. Your tongue and legs faltered and seemed to have been knitted in one knot. What then? All the staff gathered around you and started shooting anxiolytics at you. What of it? It looked like they took it for a space fever fit.

When you came to yourself in the hospital, you saw a gloomy Peleng standing at your bed. There was the following superscription on the drop-bottle, attached to your blood system: "Strong cucumber brine". You had a splitting headache and your gloomy visitor was constantly trying to dualize and run to different corners of the room.

- Hello, <Ranger>, I'm Bardozze, doctor Bardozze, by your permission, former owner of the only xenopark all over the <ToStar> system.
- Ah, hi, do you happen to have beer?
- I'm afraid I've got unpleasant news for you.

He handed a copy of the local newspaper to you. There was a huge headline staring right in the face from the front page: "Crashed <Ranger> destroyed our wonderful Bardozzes xenopark". You read the article and it fell into your mind that you'd rather been in another system and in another age. Moreover, you realised that furious locals were waiting for you under the windows of the hospital.

- What do you want? Amends?
- No, the xenopark was insured. I just don't want the reputation of a person who let the crowd tear you to pieces. It might create problems with the insurance. I'll help you to disappear from our planet and hope I'll never see you again.

With the help of Bardozze's assistants you got to your ship and forgot about the accident in an hour while preparing for the take off.
loc.46.0:
You grabbed several sprigs of the plant, carefully unthorned them and took a dollop. Thick slightly sour and acerb juice flushed into your mouth.
 
Damn it! It's Vtequila - your favourite wash-belly!
loc.47.0:
You pushed the emergency button and the care-taker together with an unknown Peleng in the expensive suit immediately entered the room.

- Let me introduce the owner of the xenopark, mister Brigee Bardozze, himself to you. This is the most respected and major businesspeleng on <ToPlanet>, - the care-taker pointed to the heavy Peleng. - And this is our rescuer, great ranger <Ranger>.
- Nice to meet you, mister Bardozze, did you have a good rest on the Cvaribbeans? - you forced out a greeting.
- Thank you, it was just wonderful, but it was the Cvanarians, not the Cvaribbeans. Thank you kindly for saving my pets, - Bardozze clasped your hand smiling, - The other part of my thanks will come from my pocket. I hope that my simple <Money> cr gift will compensate your time and nerves. Unfortunately, to get your fee you will have to fly back to <FromPlanet> - these bureaucrats require all financials issues connected with your employment to be decided through their bank. And I'll be happy to see you again in my xenopark. You are welcome and receive a special...let us say, 10% entrance fee discount! Hold on! Let it be even 11% - you are our rescuer!!!

You answered with no enthusiasm dreaming just of getting back to your ship, taking a shower and having a sleep. With that idea in your mind, you were going to the exit when the care-keeper drew up with you.
- Here, - he handed a small container to you smiling cunningly, - here is one more simple gift from mister Bardozze.
- What is it? - you asked suspiciously.
- Have a look...
You opened the container and shut it tightly again. The very sploshling was looking prankishly at you.
- This is the last one, - the Peleng commented with a happy smile and added as if reading your thoughts: - And returning a gift back is considered bad manners... Good bye. And don't forget to feed it properly.
- What kind of food... - you didn't finish the phrase because he disappeared the next moment.
loc.49.0:
There was a tablet with the superscription <clr> "Khahapt globules"<clrEnd> on Tub № 3.

There turned out to be a back full of globules under the lid. Though you didn't find Khahapt himself there. Well, probably he won't mind if you try some.

You took a couple of globules in your hand. Solid, rugged and like an egg of a furpus (or a human nail) in size, they turned out to be surprisingly fragile and you easily crumbled them. Their straw colour and tasty smell said that they might have been eatable....
loc.49.1: You ate a bellyful of the globules that turned out to be your favourite Pop-feed. Full stomach makes the brains work better - see what the food with high content of carbohydrates can do!!!
loc.49.2: You took one globule and licked it carefully. It felt like its luscious taste brought you back to your calf-time but you failed to figure out what memories were connected with that taste.
loc.49.3: You took several globules and put them on your tongue. Then you chewed them with a slight crisp and laughed: good for the Gaalians! Who in the entire Galaxy would call this favourite teenager food Khahapt globules! You knew for sure that there was no Gaalian Khahapt who had created those globules - that was a culinary triumph of the Peleng cooks, which was called Pop-feed. You used to crisp them not once yourself sitting in the stereotheater...
loc.51.0:
The tablet on Tub №4 said:
<clr>Granulated sparklings <clrEnd>

There turned out to be a lot of limpid small crystals. They were really sparkling in the light of the lamps. It must have been the authors' idea to facet the crystals.. Though may be, they were from a planet with the type of climate that had shaped them like that. There was also a possibility that those were seeds of some exotic plant of even eggs of an insectoid, though they had no smell and felt cool and rather solid.
loc.51.1:
You took a small crystal and threw it into your mouth.

There - and doctor Svaikoff guaranteed that this filling would stay forever. Though he didn't cram  - there was an untouched seal prancing on the broken tooth with the holographic label of "Svaikoff and Ga". Well, you would tell your friends that you had lost it in the battle but not while trying to scoff the food for an unknown xenomorph.
loc.51.2: You took a crystal carefully and licked it. Neither taste, not smell, just your cut tongue...
loc.52.0:
You grabbed a handful of sparklings and threw them in your mouth. The diamond-hard feed cost several broken teeth already but suddenly the door admitting to the room with the animals flew open with terrible noise and a crowd of Pelengs in the uniform rushed in carrying guns.

One of them took out a radio-set and the others pointed their dreadful barrels at you. 
- This is captain Quacksha Chuck, non-governmental security department squad, speaking. Emergency call confirmed. Location - mister Bardozze's xenopark. Reason - the security system detected a wrong trajectory of A code feed transferring. Version - an unknown ranger is trying to steal A code feed hiding it away in his oral cavity. Stopping means - object destruction.

Fire blades issued forward from the barrels and stuck into your chest. On your way to unconsciousness you heard the guards' voices:
- Well, one more A feed hunter killed. 
- May his energy essence go to Tzvackian Swales, sooner or later all of us will be there. Here, Khachick-Khan, do you know what animal are these diamonds for?..

Darkness fell upon you...
loc.55.0:
<clr>"Glandulous Noohoo-Dle"<clrEnd> was on Tub №5.

In that tub there were a lot of long thin rods looking like cords of different colours. Their surface of all kinds of colours seemed to be too smooth for a stem of a plant. May be, it really was an extract from some animal's glands as it was said on the tablet.
loc.55.1: You took the smoothest and brightest sprig (or whatever it was) and carefully licked it. The silken rind insoluble in your saliva savoured of either plastic, or quitine, or, may be, shell-horn - you were too inexperienced to guess.
loc.55.2: You put a couple of rods in the mouth and chewed. At last, when you managed to tear the rind with your teeth, they grated on the pith. It was soft but strong, tinny and reddish and completely discouraged you from experimenting any longer.
loc.55.3: The first attempt was enough to realise that you better stay your hand - the pleasure seemed to be very doubtful.
loc.57.0:
There are <clr>"Elementary Photons"<clrEnd> in Tub 6.

It is a huge piece of... a substance that stinks a lot. May be, it "has a high content of photons" as it is mentioned on the tablet, but it says nothing to you. Was it kept in the sunlight? Or do they fry photon-emitter to prepare it? Whatever it is, this cloudy green substance covered by slime made no associations appear in your head, or...almost no associations.
loc.57.1: You bent carefully over the tub and licked the mass. Suddenly it moved and started producing such fetidity that tears appeared in your eyes. But in a couple of minutes the stink was gone and it became motionless again. Just your tongue was burnt rather badly - the slime turned out to be caustic.
loc.58.0:
You picked a small piece of elementary photons and put it in the mouth...

The ranger's death was instantaneous and painless.
loc.60.0:
You threw open the lid of the last tub with <clr>Hydrocarbon tincture <clrEnd>. 

There turned out to be a bubbly dark-brown liquid with nice smell. A lot of small bubbles appeared on the bottom then emerging to the surface and popping with a quiet sound. No smell of the familiar hydrocarbons.
loc.60.1:
You dipped up some of the liquid and drank it. Nice tickling of the bubbles made you cough but you realised that it was no hydrocarbon tincture at all but ordinary cola - carbonated non-alcoholic drink, the influence of human fashion on other cuisine eagerly accepted by other races.

Your sudden hiccing scared the animals and you had to sing a lullaby to calm them down. However, it made them afraid even more..
loc.60.2: You wet your finger with the liquid and dripped a couple of drops on your tongue. It fizzed up a little, but didn't burn the tongue, just tickled it. What a familiar taste! And this tang caused by gases...
loc.65.0:
The creature was ignoring the bubbly drink for some time, then it grew bolder and sucked it up with its trunk.. The result was instantaneous  - the xenomorph started quivering and... <clr>mouldered <clrEnd>, turning into a handful of blue dust. 

Alarm siren wailed out. The scared care-taker ran into the room accompanied by a huge Maloq guard. 
- Oh, dear! - the Peleng shouted going pale.
loc.65.chg.0:
Maloq stared at the handful of blue dust that had been wheezing in the corner not long ago and took out his blaster:
- Die, the murderer of the Maloq symbol! - he shouted releasing the trigger. Bluish flame folded you and you went out of the world.
loc.67.0:
Soon the bender of xenopark disappeared beyond the horizon and the spaceport appeared ahead of you. Only then you awoke to the fact that all nightmares were over. Perhaps, it's easier for you to liberate a couple of systems from dominators than messing about with these beasts... 

After that mission you were set to dealing with humanoids only, avoiding penchequack fights and "The world of xenomorphs" program. And you will let the sploshling out of the container BY NO MEANS...
loc.68.0:
In the street you came across Rabby Terezze - the chief feeder of the xenopark.

- Ah, <Ranger>, happy to see you in good health. Judging from you appearance, you coped with it. My congratulations! By the way - I can answer all your questions and explain what creatures you dealt with - they told me over the radio-set, that the sploshling had mixed up the tablets again...

Ask, <Ranger>...
loc.68.1:
- It was the Aishout, a rather interesting plant. Completely brainless, whatever the ihike-bahanists may say, but able to shift. It absorbs amylum from starchy food and reprocesses it into glucose. And it gets carbon dioxide necessary to synthesis from the carbonated water.
- But there is no light in the cage!
- There is, it's just that the Aishout's native sun radiates light in special spectrum, which seems black to us. 

"Of all things! What a scientific base these Gaalian ihike-bahanists created for the intellect of an elementary plant!" - you thought...
loc.68.2:
- It was the Aishout, a rather interesting plant. Completely brainless, whatever the ihike-bahanists may say, but able to shift. It absorbs amylum from starchy food and reprocesses it into glucose. And it gets carbon dioxide necessary to synthesis from the carbonated water.
- But there is no light in the cage!
- There is, it's just that the Aishout's native sun radiates light in special spectrum, which seems black to us.
- I doubt its brainlessness - it buried a sprig of Quack-Tose.
- Really? It changes a lot, and then I need to do some additional research...
loc.68.3:
- Oh, that was a phatklink. They feed on curayaba, swamp heather, straining it out of the swamp. The mass that contains this heather is called criambusine.
- But it almost ate me!!!
- Phatklinks are poor sighted and it probably took you for a female and wanted to play. By the way, phatklinks are distant relations of the earth frogs. And what a nice slick warty skin they have - I love to pat it... And how they sing - "Croak! Croak!!! Cro-o-ak!" 

May be, it's time to change the topic...
loc.68.4:
- Judging from your description, it was the Klissan proto-shpock. It passed into our hands from the Klissan Galaxy...I think. An extremely unpleasant creature! It regenerates the appearance with a frightful speed. And if it's not irradiated by white lamplight, it can change its shape and even sizes. This is a very dangerous animal, I should say, and damn intellectual.
- Indeed, - you cringed. - Is it why it needs food with high content of photons?
- Photons? What photons? Oh, no - it is just a wrong translation; I keep forgetting to make new tablets. It was the protoplasm with an activating coagulant. The translator understood "plasma" as "photon", and made a mistake omitting "proto".
- And what kind of floor is there in the cage?
- This is a special material - the only type that can stop proto-shpock, it can nibble even titan armour. By the way, any human food is deadly for it... Do you have any more questions?
loc.68.5: - That was a Sand Ship, they were brought to Mars from Earth. The Martian sands turned out to be suitable for them. They call them "camels" or "dessert ships" there on Earth. And they feed on thorny cactuses (quack-tose in the Peleng language) that grow in the dessert. Ships save water and fat in their outgrowths on the back - "humps", and the substances from the quack-tose are enough for them to do without food and water for many days. There it is!
loc.68.6:
- Judging from you description, that was the "dreadful habbath", the symbol of the Maloq courage. If it had been killed, a whole bunch of those tough guys would have dropped from the clouds on you. By the way - this is a completely harmless and cowardly creature...
- But I read the reports...
- You read the Maloq reports... It was that the poor animal just fell on one of the Maloqs in the sleep - they sleep almost all the time - and smashed it. And as long as habbaths can't produce any other noise but snoring, the captain took it for laughter and considered the beast fearless, whereas it was just scared and went to the state of hypnote.
- I see. Then where does the "disguise skill" come from? And what is Noohoo-Dle? And "sparklings"? 
- Habbaths live on Taboth, in the rocks, which are of the same blue colour as the habbaths' skin due to the high content of sapphires in them. And Noohoo-Dle is the Sun nonstone. Normal copper, we didn't even remove insulation from the cords. Nonstone is iron, and "sun" is due to the fact that the Taboth sun is auburn. And we use the diamonds (or granulated sparklings) because they grind the copper to powder in the habbath's stomach. Undigested diamonds get back to us...
   
After these words you swallowed and surreptitiously wiped your hands on the uniform guessing how the habbath gives the diamonds back.

- By the way - it's good that you didn't try to steal the diamonds - they are all marked and if the trajectory of at least one of them doesn't coincide with the one specified... In general, your honesty, or just ignorance, saved your skin. Any more questions?

jump.49.desc:
Thick pseudoclouds were wreathing in the bright blue light of the sun-imitator. It was strange but the beast in the cage felt comfortless there - it quivered chilly and blebs were appearing and disappearing on its dark green skin and looked like ripple. Its both eyes were closed.

Spots of disgustingly looking slime covered the floor and drifted on the surface of multiple puddles. The creature fastidiously wiped the slime off its skin and crawled along the cage following the shade of the pseudoclouds. When it got in the shadow, it almost merged there. Two pairs of its paws finished in wide flat "palms" which could be suitable for either swimming or walking on the quick-sand. Small "suckers" could be seen on the "fingertips". You failed to distinguish in the shade if it tucked its fifth leg under it or just leaned on its tail.

Suddenly the creature opened its both eyes and stared at you. The xenomorph opened wide its chaps with three rows of small teeth. It made it look as if its flat head split to two parts. It fired its long blue tongue from the chaps, which swirled around your hand. The sucker on the tip of the tongue burst like a flower-bud and leeched to your palm. With curses you darted from the cage. The beast attached to you flew two meters in the air and banged against the cage power grid.

It fell unconscious because of the bang and let your hand go. But in a couple of minutes the creature's shapeless body lazily crawled to the shade. Its eyes were closed again. 
  
You properly washed your hands rubbing the slime off. The spots where it got were burning but there was no visible harm and after a while the itch was gone too.
jump.51.desc:
The xenomorph in the last cage turned out to look nicer than the other ones. Its long runty body with six short and bandy paws was covered with cloudy scale. The flat piked mug turned to you as soon as you approached. The xenomorph's tail was almost twice longer than the body - despite of short paws one got the impression of the creature's dangerous precipitation. 

The white shine of eight long lamps was reflected in the floor, which looked like marble or coated with some similar stone.

Its shining surface seemed like polished by vehement winds but the air in the cage was completely quiet, dry, rather warm and flavourless. Out of mere play you stepped on the tip of the tail that was lopping through the grid. The tail went off. 

You were extremely surprised when the xenomorph slowly moved away from you almost ignoring the fact of losing its organ. May be, it didn't notice anything? It looked like the beast felt no pain... To keep out of mischief you decided not to take hazards...

jump.113.text: Check the animal that became crippled ...much thanks to your unsleeping care
jump.113.desc:
Hoo!!! It didn't waste its time on trifles. At least one third of the tail grew up again. This animal can feed so many starving Chinese... What if we cut off something else from it?

Wait a minute? - you said to yourself, - did I come to feed them or to play doctor Moreau? Wannabe vivisector... 

You silently stood at the last cage and looked at the ceiling. There were only five poor hungry animals...and how much trouble they gave! To entertain yourself, you started singing but the animals didn't seem to like it so you stopped. You would never become the second Kuciano Pavalozzi...
jump.114.desc:
As soon as you came to the cage, its inhabitant lazily crawled out from the shade and stared at you. For a couple of minutes you were playing glimmers and the beast opened its chaps wide. 

Being a sadder and a wiser man, you sprang back from the cage but The beast just yawned and kept staring at you as if expecting something...
jump.129.text: Scoff a piece of the photons
jump.133.text: Examine the content of the tub with the tablet "hydrocarbon tincture"
jump.151.text: Feed it with the vazze criambusine
jump.151.desc:
You plunked a couple of handfuls near the creature. It slightly bent over the pile, then stuck its pulpi down into it and glued to the spot. You remained motionless too watching. Ten minutes passed. Neither you, not the animal made a move. An hour passed. You were out of patience, took a broom and carefully touched the xenomorph.

You heard the same sound as if you had hit a stone. Damn it, it was a stone! Your passion for experimenting <clr>killed<clrEnd> the animal.
jump.151.chg.0:
The faces of the care-takers who came at alarm betokened no good to you and you preferred to get out of there. 
And in the morning all the newspapers wrote about "...ranger <Ranger> who commemorated the last Graceful Aishout turning it into stone"

And the Green society members organised a demonstration at your spaceship: 

a crowd of green Pelengs in green uniforms were waving green slogans and threw green tomatoes at your spaceship. You could do nothing but grate your teeth and green with fury.
jump.152.text: Feed it with the granulated sparklings
jump.155.text: Treat the beast with the elementary photons
jump.156.text: Pour in some of the hydrocarbon tincture
jump.158.desc:
You threw several globules at the animal that caught them speedily. It chewed up the farinose feed crisping and even became a little bit lighter. There appeared some content in the beast's eyes or did it just seem to you? It ate several more globules with the same speed. Then it crawled to the bowl with the "tincture" - you could hear distinct rash of its either roots, or pulpi - and gladly deepened its wide paws, or, as you realised, leaves, in the liquid. 

The thinking plant <clr>is filled<clrEnd>.
jump.159.desc:
You threw several globules at the animal that caught them speedily. It chewed up the farinose feed crisping and even became a little bit lighter. There appeared some content in the beast's eyes or did it just seem to you? It ate several more globules with the same speed. Then it crawled to the bowl with the "tincture" - you could hear distinct rash of its either roots, or pulpi - and gladly deepened its wide paws, or, as you realised, leaves, in the liquid. In a couple of minutes its colour turned light - the signs of the illness disappeared, and the juice stopped dribbling from the chaps.

The thinking plant <clr>is filled<clrEnd>.
jump.160.text: Break off a sprig of quack-tose
jump.161.text: Give some quack-tose sprigs to the beast
jump.161.desc: You emptied about a dozen of thorny sprigs in front of the hungry beast. It stuck out its tongue and started palpating the feed. It shouldn't have done it. The beast skipped aside with a nasty scream when a couple of thorns entered its tongue. The xenomorph looked... <clr>sad and disappointed <clrEnd>.
jump.161.chg.0:
If the poor animal felt unwell before the accident, now it was... dead. 

You called the clerks of the xenopark and had them take care of the corpse. Naturally, they cast you out quickly. And in the next morning the following headlines were flashing from the front pages of the local newspapers: "Ranger <Ranger> bankrupted dear mister Bardozze", "Merciless killer of our dear phatklinks - who is he?..." and so on.

The only good thing about these newspapers - they are pretty soft. And there is nothing more valuable during a long hyperjump than a lot of good food and soft toilet...sorry, newspaper.
jump.162.text: Plunk a bit of criambusine for it
jump.162.desc: You put the criambusine in the manger and stepped aside. The beast crawled out of the shade and approached the manger. Its long tongue palpated the feed; the creature produced a joyful "Croak!!!" and started grabbing the criambusine with its lips and slowly chewing it. That's it! The creature is <clr>filled and happy <clrEnd>.
jump.163.text: Feed the beast with the Noohoo-Dle
jump.165.desc: The creature accepted the bubbling of the dark-brown liquid with joy and started lapping it with its long tongue. But in a couple of minutes it crawled aside. It looked like it had a hissing fit - it was quivering and time to time jumped with a loud "qq-qua-ka" jerking its paws in a funny way. The tincture <clr>did it no good <clrEnd>.
jump.165.chg.0:
Damn it, it was the last straw and the sick animal looked much worse. Its paws faltered and it plunked on the floor. The xenomorph jolted in agony a couple of times and became quiet. Forever.

You called the clerks of the xenopark and had them take care of the corpse. Naturally, they cast you out quickly. And in the next morning the following headlines were flashing from the front pages of the local newspapers: "Ranger <Ranger> bankrupted dear mister Bardozze", "Merciless killer of our dear phatklinks - who is he?..." and so on.

The only good thing about these newspapers - they are pretty soft. And there is nothing more valuable during a long hyperjump than a lot of good food and soft toilet...sorry, newspaper.
jump.166.text: Treat the ranger-eater with the Khahapt globules
jump.167.text: Treat it with the Khahapt globules
jump.168.text: Threw the elementary photons at it
jump.168.desc: A piece of the elementary photons fell with a spat near the creature. Well, the photons were not as elementary as they promised - as soon as the creature touched the clot with its tongue, it started <clr>expending before your eyes until it burst<clrEnd>.
jump.168.chg.0:
You decided to belt off from the xenopark out of harm's way but the caretaker met you in the corridor. He noticed your dirty uniform. - Just don't tell me that you tried to inflate the phatklink through a straw, - he maliciously said between his teeth.

- Get out of here and never show up on <ToPlanet> again, ranger <Ranger>.
jump.169.desc:
The creature crawled up to the bowl with the "tincture" - you could hear distinct rash of its either roots, or pulpi - and gladly deepened its wide paws, or, as you realised, leaves, into the liquid. 

It looked like <clr>that was all the beast needed to be completely happy <clrEnd>.
jump.171.desc:
You hardly went away from the cage when the creature rolled up to the scattering of sparklings and scrambled it up in a pile with its either trunk, or palpus that appeared as if growing out from the body. Then it stretched its trunk (or pulpus? Or snoot?) towards the sparklings and... sucked them in. At last the animal rolled away to the far corner and fell asleep.
    
Cell...oh, Cage №4 habitant is <clr>filled<clrEnd>.
jump.173.text: Share a piece of photons with the xenomorph
jump.175.text: Thrust a bunch of Noohoo-Dle to the xenomorph
jump.176.text: Thrust a bunch of Noohoo-Dle to the xenomorph
jump.176.desc:
You will never understand these creatures - you hardly stretched out your hand when the animal rolled up to you and grabbed the Noohoo-Dle with its either trunk, or palpus that appeared as if growing out from the body. After sucking the wriggly rods in, it stretched its snoot (or trunk?) towards the pile of crystals and sucked them in too. Then it rolled away to the corner and fell asleep.

It looked like the blue-skinned dormouse is <clr>filled<clrEnd>.
jump.177.text: Throw several Khahapt globules to the beast
jump.178.text: Treat the animal with the criambusine
jump.181.text: Thank you, I have already straightened out the whole thing
jump.188.text: Feed the animal with the criambusine
jump.189.text: Feed the xenomorph with the hydrocarbon tincture
jump.189.desc: The beast approached the drinking-bowl and started greedily lapping the liquid with its forked tongue. Suddenly it quivered and... <clr>gave, turning into a pile of brown stinking slime <clrEnd>.
jump.189.chg.0:
You hardly left the room trying to escape when the caretaker accompanied by an known Peleng ran to you. Their faces betokened no good to you:
- Oh, dear, I'm a bankrupt!!! - the unknown Peleng who turned out to be the owner of the xenopark shouted. - This freak killed the unique species of a Klissan animal. My hat! He tried to feed a creature from the Klissan Galaxy with the earth food!!! Get out, <Ranger>, until I call the police and accused you of killing the valuable animal.
jump.190.text: Pour in the Khahamp globules into the manger
jump.190.desc: The beast approached the manger and took several globules. Suddenly it quivered and... <clr>gave, turning into a pile of brown stinking slime <clrEnd>.

jump.191.text: Treat the pangolin with the Noohoo-Dle
jump.192.text: Feed the xenomorph with the sparklings
jump.193.text: Put some sprigs of the Quack-Tose into the cage
jump.194.text: Pick off a piece of food with high content of photons
jump.194.desc:
The disgusting clot of the substance hardly reached the floor when the beast darted to it and scoffed in one swallow. Its appearance changed immediately - slime started dribbling through the scale, thorns and warts covered the tail, and the number of legs was constantly changing. Suddenly its tail became three times longer and the xenomorph hit one of the lamps with it. But the lamp turned out to be hit-proofed and remained unbroken. After several more attempts to break it the creature stopped, rolled itself into a ball and became motionless. 

Well, <clr>the monster is filled <clrEnd>...
jump.197.desc:
Thick pseudoclouds were wreathing in the bright blue light of the sun-imitator. It was strange but the beast in the cage felt comfortless there - it quivered chilly and blebs were appearing and disappearing on its dark green skin and looked like ripple. Its both eyes were closed.

Spots of disgustingly looking slime covered the floor and drifted on the surface of multiple puddles. The creature fastidiously wiped the slime off its skin and crawled along the cage following the shade of the pseudoclouds. When it got in the shadow, it almost merged there. Two pairs of its paws finished in wide flat "palms" which could be suitable for either swimming or walking on the quick-sand. Small "suckers" could be seen on the "fingertips". You failed to distinguish in the shade if it tucked its fifth leg under it or just leaned on its tail.
jump.199.text: Examine the cage inhabitant once again
jump.199.desc:
The xenomorph in the last cage turned out to look nicer than the other ones. Its long runty body with six short and bandy paws was covered by cloudy scale. The flat piked mug turned to you as soon as you approached. The xenomorph's tail used to be almost twice longer than the body but now it was just a stub of a tail.

The white shine of eight long lamps was reflected in the floor, which looked like marble or coated with some similar stone. Its shining surface seemed like polished by vehement winds but the air in the cage was completely quiet, dry, rather warm and flavourless
jump.200.text: Don't stare and confuse the animal
jump.201.text: Read the books if you have some spare time...
